clue.text: Unconventional greeting by Frenchman a strain

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for Monsieur, a Frenchman's title
ave is the Latin word of greeting, hail
a rick is a sprain or strain, as in a ricked neck

explanation.surface: A Frenchman offers an odd hello while straining himself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' only places the greeting beside the Frenchman; the pieces run M, AVE, RICK.
explanation.definitionFit: A maverick is an independent-minded person who refuses to conform, hence unconventional.

clue.text: Penny prize defective in Edwardian times

parts.note: P is the abbreviation for a penny in British money

indicators.note: defective means lacking a part, so the word for prize loses its final letter

parts.note: a reward is a prize given for something done

explanation.surface: A cheap prize turns out faulty in the early years of the twentieth century.
explanation.walkthrough: 'defective' drops the last letter of the prize word. The Edwardian era (1901-1910) came just before the First World War.
explanation.definitionFit: The Edwardian period immediately preceded the 1914 conflict, so it lies before the war.

clue.text: With no delay, materiel getting processed

indicators.note: processing works raw material into a new form, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Military equipment is handled immediately.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting processed' rearranges the eight letters of MATERIEL.
explanation.definitionFit: Computing done in real time happens instantly, as events occur, without any lag.

clue.text: Keep pushing, getting closer

definitions.meaning: to keep pushing or butting is to ..., as to keep going is to go on
a fastener that closes a garment, such as a shirt's

explanation.walkthrough: 'getting' links the two senses; 'closer' is a thing that closes, not 'nearer'.
explanation.definitionFit: A button closes a coat, so it is a closer; and butting on means continuing to push.

clue.text: Request for typically American dish? That's neat

definitions.meaning: an order placed for apple pie, a dish thought of as typically American
tidy and orderly in every detail

explanation.walkthrough: 'That's' links the two senses. Apple pie is proverbially American ('as American as apple pie').
explanation.definitionFit: Being in apple-pie order is an idiom for being perfectly neat and tidy.

clue.text: Characteristic pastry I bit into then rejected

indicators.note: rejected means turned back, so the assembled letters are read in reverse order
I goes inside the pastry, as a bite goes into it

parts.note: a tart is a pastry case with a filling

explanation.surface: Someone's typical habit: biting into a pastry and then spitting it out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bit into' puts I inside TART to give TIART, and 'then rejected' turns that round.
explanation.definitionFit: A trait is a distinguishing feature or quality of someone's character.

clue.text: What offers magnified view of jumbo worker abandoned — completely?

indicators.note: the trimmed jumbo is placed within the word for completely, as part of it

parts.note: toto, from the Latin phrase in toto, means completely

indicators.note: the worker is abandoned, dropped from the end of the jumbo word

parts.note: Jumbo was a famous elephant, and the word stands for any elephant
an ant is the standard crossword worker, from the worker ant

explanation.surface: A question about seeing an elephant up close, with a worker left behind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abandoned' drops the worker from the end of the jumbo word; 'of' sets what remains inside the Latin word, the 'in' of in toto suggesting the containment.
explanation.definitionFit: A telephoto lens is designed to give an enlarged image of distant subjects.

clue.text: Two examples of money used to correspond

parts.note: a banknote is an example of money
paper money is another form of currency

explanation.surface: Two kinds of money spent on letter-writing.
explanation.walkthrough: One phrase gives both pieces: a note and paper are both money.
explanation.definitionFit: Writing paper is what people use for letters, i.e. to correspond.

clue.text: Selected item from Paris

definitions.meaning: the French word for a thing or item

explanation.walkthrough: 'from Paris' signals a French word.
explanation.definitionFit: To pick is to choose, past tense chose; in French, chose means thing.

clue.text: Midwife's unsympathetic advice?

parts.note: a midwife telling a mother in labour to smile and carry the baby to birth, read as the idiom for enduring trouble stoically

explanation.walkthrough: 'bear' is read as giving birth, not as tolerating.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means put up with something unpleasant without complaint, here given a birthing twist.

clue.text: Saying nothing about home record

indicators.note: the silent word goes around the home word

parts.note: mute means silent, saying nothing
in means at home

explanation.surface: Keeping quiet about the house's record.
explanation.walkthrough: 'record' looks like a noun but works as the verb, to write down officially.
explanation.definitionFit: To minute a meeting is to record it in official notes.

clue.text: Sad few months for US leads to collapse

parts.note: down means low in spirits
fall is the American word for autumn, a season of a few months

explanation.surface: A gloomy American autumn brings about a breakdown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leads to' links the pieces to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A downfall is a ruin or collapse, as of a regime.

clue.text: Basic character a sort of reserve

explanation.walkthrough: 'reserve' suggests shyness, but it is the type of protected area.
explanation.definitionFit: A person's nature is their essential temperament; a nature reserve protects wildlife.

clue.text: Man, wife and son make overture

parts.note: he stands for a man as the male pronoun
a bride is a newly married wife

explanation.surface: A family of husband, wife and son making an opening approach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'make' links the pieces to the definition. The Hebrides is Mendelssohn's concert overture, also called Fingal's Cave.
explanation.definitionFit: Mendelssohn named his famous overture after these Scottish islands.

clue.text: Army on manoeuvres bypassing philosopher, in general

indicators.note: the shuffled letters go past, around either side of, the philosopher
an army on manoeuvres moves about, so its letters, with on, are reshuffled

parts.note: Immanuel Kant was the German philosopher

explanation.surface: An army on exercise avoids a thinker while serving under a commander.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on manoeuvres' makes MARONY, which 'bypassing' wraps round the philosopher. 'in' is a link; 'general' looks like an adjective but is the soldier.
explanation.definitionFit: Mark Antony was the Roman general and ally of Julius Caesar.

clue.text: Through violence, is arrested at the front

indicators.note: at the front of each word, so the opening letters of three words are taken

explanation.surface: Arrest follows violence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at the front' takes V, I, A from the three words.
explanation.definitionFit: Via means by way of or through, as in travelling via London.

clue.text: Withdraw tyre that needs changing finally

indicators.note: the final letter of the tyre word is changed, the T coming from the end of that

parts.note: a retread is a tyre given a new tread

explanation.surface: Pull back the tyre that's worn out at the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'needs changing finally' swaps the last letter D of RETREAD for T, the last letter of 'that'.
explanation.definitionFit: To retreat is to pull back or withdraw, as an army does.

clue.text: Broken toy: policeman to start to feature?

indicators.note: a broken toy is in pieces, so these letters are put together differently

explanation.surface: A policeman is about to appear in a story about a smashed toy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Broken' rearranges TOY and POLICEMAN, twelve letters; 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To come into play is to become relevant or begin to have an effect.

clue.text: In summary, slightly exaggerate what's beside the point

definitions.meaning: a digest of news or events

definitions.text: slightly exaggerate what's beside the point
definitions.meaning: to raise a figure to the next whole number, overstating what follows the decimal point

explanation.walkthrough: 'In' is a link. 'beside the point' means after the decimal point, not irrelevant.
explanation.definitionFit: A news round-up is a summary; rounding up a decimal slightly overstates it.

clue.text: Picture of rare cow left out for review

indicators.note: a review recasts material, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A painting of an unusual cow is omitted from the art critics' list.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for review' rearranges RARE, COW, L and OUT, eleven letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A watercolour is a painting done in water-based paints.

clue.text: No good to smooth thick skin

indicators.note: no means without, so the good letter is removed

parts.note: to grind something is to wear it smooth

explanation.surface: Polishing won't help a tough hide.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No' takes G away from GRIND.
explanation.definitionFit: The rind is the tough outer layer of fruit, cheese or bacon.

clue.text: Flier, arrested, took to the water in America

parts.note: collared is slang for arrested by the police

parts.words: took to the water in America
parts.note: dove is the American past tense of dive

explanation.surface: A pilot is nabbed by police after plunging into water in the States.
explanation.walkthrough: Americans say 'dove' where Britons say 'dived'.
explanation.definitionFit: The collared dove is a common bird, so a flier.

clue.text: Maybe world representative has put down a European dynasty

indicators.note: in a down entry, putting the letter down moves it further along the word

parts.note: a world is an example of a planet, as Maybe signals
an agent acts as a representative
E is the abbreviation for European

explanation.surface: A planetary envoy deposes a European royal line.
explanation.walkthrough: PLANETAGENT has its E moved down, past the following letters, to just before the last T.
explanation.definitionFit: The Plantagenets were the royal house that ruled England from 1154 to 1485.

clue.text: The rich have influence in economics lectures?

definitions.meaning: wealth buys power, as the saying goes
talks given about money, read literally

explanation.walkthrough: The second sense reads the saying literally as lectures on money.
explanation.definitionFit: The saying means wealth gives people power; literally, it is talks about cash.

clue.text: Grossmiths' diarist finds home for one old dog

indicators.note: the home word stands in for one of the two old letters

parts.note: Charles Pooter is the diarist in The Diary of a Nobody by George and Weedon Grossmith
in means at home

explanation.surface: A fictional diarist finds a home for an old hound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for one' puts IN in place of one O in POOTER. 'finds' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A pointer is a gun dog that points at game.

clue.text: Not so generous, supporting Conservative daily

indicators.note: in a down entry, a supporting piece sits below the other

parts.note: leaner means less ample, not so generous

explanation.surface: A stingier politician props up the Tory newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: A daily is British slang for a cleaner who comes in each day; 'daily' looks like a newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: A daily is a domestic help who comes in to clean, so a cleaner.

clue.text: Sign here, people!

parts.note: O is the vocative cry used to call attention, like here!
men stands for people

explanation.surface: A call for everyone to put their names down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sign' looks like a verb asking for a signature; it is a portent.
explanation.definitionFit: An omen is a sign or portent of things to come.

clue.text: What controls our inheritance comes up also here

indicators.note: in a down entry, coming up means read from bottom to top

parts.note: DNA carries the genetic code we inherit

explanation.surface: Genetics surfaces here as well.
explanation.walkthrough: 'comes up' turns DNA round; 'here' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: And joins added items, meaning also or in addition.
